newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Three groups to bid for four Sri Lanka estate firm.
newsitem.headline: Three groups to bid for four Sri Lanka estate firm.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Thursday that three groups have qualified to bid for strategic holdings in four plantation firms, which the government will sell on the stock exchange from July 4.

"A consortium with Aitken Spence & Co is one of the bidders. The other two led, by Forbes Ceylon Ltd and Wayamba Plantations Ltd, have also been pre-qualified to bid for 51 percent stakes in Malwatte, Kahawatte, Elpitiya and Elkaduwa plantations firms," said an official from the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), who declined to be identified.
The PERC said last month that Malwatte Plantations would be sold on July 4, followed by Kahawatte on July 7, Elpitiya on July 8 and Elkaduwa a day later.
Malwatte will be introduced at a minimum price of 40 rupees per 10-rupee share. The other three will come at a minimum price of 30 rupees for each 10-rupee share, the official said.
Sri Lanka began restructuring its ailing plantation sector by privatising management of 23 plantation firms, which own some 600,000 hecatres of tea, rubber and coconut land, in 1992.
Privatisation began in 1995 when it sold 51 percent or 10.2 million shares to a strategic investor, gave 10 percent to workers and sold the balance to the public.
The government retains one "golden" share, which empowers it to intervene in case of mismanagement.
